summary: South Africa admits most Western passports visa-free — 90 days for the US, UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, Brazil and Russia, and 30 days for several others — while nationalities such as China and India need a visa, which they can now also get online through the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) for arrival at four international airports. Home Affairs requires at least one blank passport page for endorsements.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 30 days after your intended departure from South Africa and have at least one unused page for entry and departure endorsements, according to Home Affairs. The UK government says British passports need at least 2 blank pages.

vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if your journey starts in, or passes through, the yellow fever belt of Africa or South America. Only direct transit through such an area is exempt.

declarations.submitWindow: Before you travel, for entry and for departure
declarations.text: From 1 July 2026 every traveller entering or leaving South Africa by air, land or sea must submit a customs traveller declaration online before travelling, unless a limited paper-based exception applies. Submit it on the SARS website, the SATMS app or the SARS MobiApp, one per traveller including children, and keep the emailed confirmation to show customs officers.

source.name: South African Revenue Service — Customs Online Traveller Declaration

currencyLimits.text: Carrying more than R100,000 in South African banknotes, or foreign currency worth more than R100,000, into or out of South Africa needs written permission from the South African Reserve Bank. Declaring the cash you carry is voluntary, on the online traveller declaration or the paper form TD-01.

source.name: South African Revenue Service — Travellers (excess currency)

notes: Home Affairs' advisory on children (revised November 2019) says unaccompanied minors of any nationality, and South African children, must on request produce documents at a port of entry, including a copy of the birth certificate and parental consent letters, and that foreign children applying for a South African visa must submit these documents with the application.

The South African Revenue Service allows each traveller to bring in duty-free no more than 200 cigarettes and 20 cigars, 250 g of tobacco, 2 litres of wine and 1 litre in total of other alcoholic beverages; under-18s get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.

payments.text: No official source we read describes card acceptance in South Africa. The UK FCDO warns that card skimming is widespread and advises changing large sums only in banks or secure shopping malls.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says there is a high crime rate in South Africa, including carjacking and 'smash and grab' attacks on vehicles at junctions, and that violent crime can take place anywhere, with the threat higher after dark. It advises keeping car doors locked and windows closed, especially at junctions, and booking taxis through internationally recognised e-hailing apps.

source.name: UK FCDO — South Africa travel advice: safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official seasonal guidance. The UK FCDO says there is a year-round risk of flooding across South Africa and that wildfires can happen in hot, dry weather, including around Cape Town; check the South African Weather Service for alerts.

idp.text: South Africa is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: South Africa is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. No official source we could read states whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, or for how long a foreign license may be used.

tips.text: The Department of Home Affairs requires at least one blank page in your passport for entry and departure endorsements; UK travel advice asks for two.

Home Affairs says unaccompanied minors of any nationality must on request produce documents at the port of entry, including a copy of the birth certificate and parental consent letters, and foreign children applying for a visa must submit them with the application.

If you drive, the Government of Canada says traffic drives on the left, advises driving defensively and avoiding travel after dark, and recommends a rental company with a 24-hour emergency service. It also advises keeping windows closed and doors locked at all times.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders get a free visitor's permit on arrival for stays of up to 90 days. You do need a passport valid for 30 days beyond departure with at least one blank page, and a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How many blank passport pages does South Africa require?
faq.answer: At least one blank page for entry and departure endorsements, according to the Department of Home Affairs; UK travel advice says two.

faq.question: What documents do children need to enter South Africa?
faq.answer: Home Affairs' advisory (revised November 2019) says the listed documents, including a copy of the birth certificate and parental consent letters, must be produced on request at a port of entry by South African children and by unaccompanied minors of any nationality, and that foreign children applying for a South African visa must submit them with the application. The UK FCDO says there are special requirements for children aged 17 and under.

faq.question: Do Chinese and Indian citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: Yes. Neither is on Home Affairs' visa exemption list for ordinary passports. Home Affairs piloted the Electronic Travel Authorisation (eta.dha.gov.za) during South Africa's G20 Presidency for travellers from China, India, Indonesia and Mexico and launched it officially on 12 August 2026: approved travellers receive it within 24 hours, and it is initially available for arrivals at OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports. Home Affairs says it will progressively become compulsory for short visits from countries that need port-of-entry visas.

faq.question: Is South Africa safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says there is a high crime rate in South Africa and reports violent attacks on hikers in Table Mountain National Park, widespread card skimming, and violence linked to tensions between e-hailing and metered taxi drivers. The Government of Canada says travel on foot is inadvisable in most areas and advises avoiding travel after dark.
